messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATION: High QPS spike for org 'hyperion' detected. Symptoms: elevated 429s and tail latency on /v1/generate. Router anomalies flagged. Pager-> ashwin_oncall.
oncall-bot: Details: 2026-07-12 14:12Z, spike_start ~14:09Z, peak qps ~4200 across 8 servers, org share ~58% of sustained burst. Error ratio 5.6%. Links: https://infra.internal/alerts/1840012345
ashwin_oncall: Picking this up. seeing the same in per-org metrics. Hyperion correlation with streaming endpoints + long context requests.
maya_sre: Quick ask — is this traffic coming from dev or prod token? Sam, can you confirm from CS?
sam_support: Confirmed with customer: prod traffic. They say they rolled out a batch async job around 14:05 that fan-outted many small requests, total concurrency got out of hand. Customer impacted? yes, some requests hitting 429 / degraded latency. They've paused their job now.
nashwin_oncall: Ok. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Apply conservative tenant-level throttle for hyperion to reduce downstream load. 2) Disable non-essential features (autocomplete & reranking) for that org via feature-flags. 3) If needed, route to a smaller-capacity model variant to shed cost.
elaine_eng: I can flip feature flags. Recommend tenant throttle to 50 rps (soft) and 200 burst to avoid client retries tearing things down. Also we should lower per-request max length to 2048 tokens for this org for now.
nashwin_oncall: Agreed. I'll run the rate adjust. Running admin command:
```
# org throttle (soft enforcement)
redwood-admin org set-throttle --org hyperion --qps 50 --burst 200 --reason "emergency spike 14:12Z"
```
nashwin_oncall: Executed. Returned: {"status":"queued","op_id":"op-9f3a"} I'm applying feature flags next.
elaine_eng: Applying feature flags now:
```
# disable autocomplete and reranking for hyperion
redwood-admin feature-flag set --org hyperion --flags disable_autocomplete,disable_rerank --actor elaine_eng
```
elaine_eng: Flags applied. Confirmed via feature flag service, snapshot id ff-20260712-001.
maya_sre: Observability check: beginning to see drop in qps to ~900 over the last 30s. Error rate trending down to 1.8%. Good. Can we also apply request-size cap?
nashwin_oncall: Applying request token cap (soft):
```
redwood-admin org set-param --org hyperion --param max_input_tokens --value 2048 --soft true
```
nashwin_oncall: Applied.
ops_lead: Heads up — enabling these mitigations will likely surface backend retries and some downstream client errors. Sam, can you craft a short message to the customer? Keep it apologetic and say we applied temporary throttles to protect their service.
sam_support: Drafting now: "Hi Hyperion team — we detected a rapid traffic increase that affected service performance. We've applied temporary rate limiting and disabled non-critical features to stabilize traffic. Please keep your paused job paused for 30 mins while we monitor. We'll follow up with a postmortem." Want me to send?
nashwin_oncall: Send it. Also ask for an ETA on when they'll resume.
sam_support: Sent. Customer acknowledged, ETA unknown.
maya_sre: Monitoring dashboards: 14:18Z CPU on serving hosts dropping, p95 latency returning to baseline. Still seeing a handful of 429s but downtrending.
elaine_eng: Rolling a fallback routing rule in case the org surges again: route to low-cost quantized model "redwood-small-q4" for requests hitting >100 token tail latency threshold. Command: 
```
redwood-admin routing add --org hyperion --condition "latency>1000ms" --model redwood-small-q4 --priority 50 --ttl 600
```
elaine_eng: Rule added.
nashwin_oncall: Can we step down throttles gradually? Recommend bump to 75 qps in 15 minutes if metrics stable.
maya_sre: Agreed. We'll schedule a bump. Setting reminder.
ops_lead: I'm going to prepare an incident brief for the PST follow-up: include timeline, mitigations, customer comms, ops actions. Assign to elaine_eng and ashwin_oncall to own postmortem.
elain_eng: small typo in participant name, but ack. I'll own the postmortem write-up with ashwin.
sam_support: Customer asked if we can provide a list of requests dropped/429s for root cause. We can provide aggregated counts and example request IDs — will coordinate offline with privacy.
maya_sre: Final check 14:25Z: qps ~240, errors ~0.3%, latency at baseline. Leaving throttles in place for another 25m, then we'll rollback if stable.
oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied: org throttle (50 qps), feature flags (autocomplete/rerank disabled), request token cap (2048), fallback routing rule. Incident severity: Sev3 -> monitoring. Handing off to day oncall.
ashwin_oncall: Handoff notes: everything applied, op_id op-9f3a for throttle change, ff snapshot ff-20260712-001. Postmortem owners: elaine_eng, ashwin_oncall.
ops_lead: Thanks everyone. If we get any regression or customer escalation, page me. Closing thread for live ops, will open postmortem in #postmortems with timeline. :thumbsup:
